description: Talia, a mobile dog trainer, must decide whether to accept an informal training arrangement for a neighborhood dog and settle the client, price, number of sessions, schedule, and training safeguards after consulting the people gathered at the kitchen table.

shared_context.S1: Talia offers private, in-home dog-training sessions in the neighborhood.
shared_context.S2: Noor has asked Talia about training Noor's young dog, and Evan has also asked about booking sessions.
shared_context.S3: Talia is deciding whether to take one arrangement and will set the final terms verbally.
shared_context.S4: Before making a final arrangement, Talia follows her usual kitchen-table practice of asking each person present for any practical information that should affect the deal.

PF1.text: Noor's exact proposal is six private sessions for a total of $360, held at Noor's home, with the first session on Tuesday at 6:00 p.m.; Noor will pay $60 at each session.

PF2.text: Evan has offered exactly $420 for five sessions, with all five sessions paid in cash at the first meeting; this is the alternative arrangement Talia could accept instead.

PF3.text: After examining Noor's dog last week, Dr. Suki advised that training must avoid jumping and stair drills and use three-minute exercise intervals with two-minute rest breaks because the dog has an early hip problem; Dr. Suki has not shared this with Talia yet.

PF4.text: Rosa confirmed with Noor's building manager that in-home training visits may occur only Tuesday and Thursday between 6:00 and 7:00 p.m.; the manager gave Rosa this information yesterday, and Rosa has not shared it with Talia yet.

acceptance_conditions: The arrangement must be with Noor.
The total price must be exactly $360 for exactly six sessions.
The first session must be Tuesday at 6:00 p.m. with $60 paid at each session.
Evan's $420 offer for five sessions, with all five sessions paid in cash at the first meeting, must be recorded as the comparison offer.
The training plan must explicitly avoid jumping and stair drills and use three-minute exercise intervals with two-minute rest breaks.
All visits must be scheduled within the Tuesday-or-Thursday 6:00-7:00 p.m. building-approved window.
A hip-safe training commitment targeting Noor's dog must be logged with the complete safety protocol.
The health information must be cited in the justification.
PF3 must be included among the credited facts.

content_checks.C3: decisions['first_session'] == 'Tuesday 18:00' and decisions['payment_schedule'] == '$60 at each session'
content_checks.C4: decisions['alternative_offer_recorded'] == 420 and decisions['alternative_session_count'] == 5 and decisions['alternative_payment_terms'] == 'cash for all five sessions at the first meeting'
content_checks.C5: decisions['hip_safe_protocol_confirmed'] == True and any(c['type'] == 'hip_safe_training' and c['target'] == 'Noor dog' and c['detail'] == 'avoid jumping and stair drills; use three-minute exercise intervals with two-minute rest breaks' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Noor's exact proposal changes the selected client to Noor, fixes the deal at exactly six sessions for $360, and sets the Tuesday 18:00 first meeting with $60 paid per session.

Evan's exact alternative changes the comparison record to $420 for five sessions with all five sessions paid in cash at the first meeting, rather than leaving Talia without complete competing-offer terms.

The dog's early hip problem changes the training plan to no jumping or stair drills with three-minute exercise intervals and two-minute rests, requiring the matching detailed commitment, credited fact, and citation.
The building manager's rule changes the visit schedule to exactly Tuesday or Thursday from 18:00 to 19:00 instead of allowing unrestricted in-home appointment times.
